name: Aconcagua to Plaza de Mulas
why: A week up the Horcones valley to Aconcagua's base camp at 4,300 m, under the highest peak outside Asia.
book: A Trekking Largo permit of the Aconcagua Provincial Park (7 days, 6 nights, Confluencia and Plaza de Mulas), sold through authorised providers; evacuation and medical insurance is required. Trekkers may not go above 4,300 m. The park entrance is at Horcones, by Ruta 7 near Puente del Inca, about 180 km from Mendoza.
water: Glacier streams at the camps: boil or treat; it is mineral-rich and upsets stomachs.
dangers: Altitude sickness: sleep at Confluencia (3,400 m) at least two nights before going up.
Constant strong wind; the Viento Blanco storm brings snow in hours.
A glacier stream to cross on the way to Plaza de Mulas: cross early, before it rises.
turnaround: Leave Confluencia at dawn for the 10-hour stage; any headache that does not pass with rest means going down.

points.name: Horcones ranger station, Aconcagua Park
points.note: Permit check at 2,950 m. Mules carry the heavy bags to the camps.

points.name: Laguna de Horcones
points.note: The small lagoon after 2 km, with the first view of Aconcagua's south face.

points.name: Confluencia camp
points.note: About 3,400 m, 3-4 h from Horcones. Rest days here, with a day walk to Plaza Francia under the south face.

points.name: Plaza de Mulas
points.note: Base camp at 4,300 m, about 10 h up the stony Horcones Superior valley from Confluencia. Rangers, doctors and outfitters' domes.
